proof.criterion: Review finding 2: a kept decision is forgotten only when the start or catch-up that named it is delivered
proof.surface: The Legion daemon outbox supervise start branch and catch-up notice publish, with the record store on real PostgreSQL
proof.command: go test -count=1 -run 'TestOnlyADeliveredStartForgetsTheDecisionsItNamed|TestOnlyADeliveredCatchUpForgetsTheDecisionsItNamed' ./internal/daemon/ ; go test -count=1 -run 'TestAParkedDecisionKeepsTheNewestPerRefAndIsForgottenOnlyWhereItWasNamed|TestAReadmittedApprovalIsKeptUntilTheStartThatNamedItIsDelivered' ./internal/record/ (inside the whole-package runs above)
proof.observed: PASS. A start or catch-up that finishes without delivering leaves the rows, and the next one names them again. A delivered start, or a published catch-up, forgets exactly the (root, ref, at) it named. A newer decision on the same ref survives the forget.
proof.negativeControl: The old code deleted the rows inside ParkedDecisionTask (TakeParkedDecisions). The new record tests assert that the rows are still present after a named but undelivered task, which that code fails by construction.

proof.negativeControl: Before the fix, step 1 had no branch for a lingering in_progress root, and the relay checked no status (thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xtcYE).

trickyParts: Forget matches on (root, ref, at), so a newer decision upserted on the same ref after the naming survives.
DropCatchUps is back to main's signature: rows now stay until delivery, so nothing has to be carried from a dropped catch-up.
deviations: A start that finds the root's architect already running names kept decisions twice: once in the catch-up from its running-claim ready, and once in its own task. Telling them twice is the at-least-once side of not losing them.
parkDecision marks the row's dedupe key processed for every outcome, so a rerun of a not-relayed row logs 'already sent'.
Under gates.design off, a kept readmitted approval is never named or forgotten. Each later keep replaces it, so there is at most one row per root.
